verdict.rationale: Carta documents creating draft option grants, which exist in a state 'that has not yet received board consent and approval.' It also documents retrieving fair market values determined by the issuer's 409A valuations, so the core pieces of the workflow exist in the product. However, the evidence never shows the board approval flow itself or strike prices being set from the 409A FMV inside one end-to-end issuance workflow. Missing for 10: a documented board consent/approval workflow, automatic 409A-based strike price assignment, end-to-end new-hire grant issuance through to an approved grant, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, I can issue options to a new hire with a board approval flow and a 409A-compliant strike price in one end-to-end workflow

citations.quote: A draft option grant is an option grant that is either still being finalized or that has not yet received board consent and approval.
Retrieve the fair market values of an issuer, which are the values of the issuer's securities as determined by the issuer's 409a valuations.
Access ownership, stakeholder lists, SAFEs, convertible notes, option grants, 409A valuations, financing history, compensation benchmarks, and more
